chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: Leaving Calloway, waiting for Duke, and being fired by Lucky Millinder
summary: Ellington asked him to wait for him; meanwhile Millinder hired him then fired him after three weeks, the only firing of his life.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Hey, let's go on to some of the bands, now, that you had played with. Your reputation of playing and supporting in making great bands sound good is longer than any other sideman that I know of.
So the last band we talked about that you had been in was what?
Was Calloway.
Calloway's band. And you left Calloway. Where'd you go? You went to Basie?
No.
Where'd you go?
When I left Calloway there was a long lull in between --
Uh-huh.

-- because Duke had talked to me and Duke told me not to take -- When he went to Europe that time, he left the band here, and he went to Europe, I think he figured some of the guys wouldn't be there when he got back or one or two of them that he didn't want to be there. And he told me not to take no regular job with anybody, you see, but to wait till he came back.
Uh-huh.

So I got a job with Lucky Millinder. Lucky Millinder had a very good band, a great band. However, I stayed there, I think it was three weeks and I got fired, the only time I ever was fired in my life. But Lucky told me I was a great trombone player, I was a gentleman, and he liked me very much, he said, but he was looking for something. And he said until he found it, he was going to still fire different guys, and he said, 'In the event that I realize that I have made a mistake in firing you, I will gladly take you back.'
That's beautiful.
You know? And he fired me and Gene Simon at the same time.
Who was Gene Simon? A saxophone player?
No, trombone player.
Oh, Gene Simon.
Yeah. We was in Don's band together.
I see.
See, Gene Simon took Claude Jones' place with Don Redman back in '33 when Claude left.
Claude left to go with Fletcher then, huh?
Went back to Fletcher.
I see.
And he played with Chick for a while, too.
We were talking about --
